Apple further detailed its Apple Music AI labeling requirements, which were first announced back in March.

AI-generated content on Apple Music will be clearly labeled

Apple previously announced that Apple Music will require AI transparency disclosures for new cover art, songs, compositions, and music videos uploaded to the platform.

The company further explained how this measure will work today.

Apple stated in an email sent to creators today: "Later this year, we will display these markers on the Apple Music user interface with a 'Made With AI' label."

Apple has also clarified the situations in which disclosures are required. The email content is as follows:

Apple Music added that this measure aims to "provide listeners with the greatest possible transparency" and directed creators to refer to its Music Style Guide for more information.

Apple Music's approach is only the latest example of streaming platforms responding to the surge of AI-generated music—an increasing number of artists are incorporating generative AI into their production processes.

Spotify previously stated that it will, by default, exclude music from AI Personas from its editorial and algorithmic recommendations; Deezer also announced last year that songs fully generated by AI will not be included in recommendations or editorial playlists. Deezer revealed last month that music fully generated by AI accounted for over half of total daily new uploads for the first time.

Taking Apple Music as an example, platform head Oliver Schusser mentioned in an earlier interview with Billboard's "On the Record" podcast that although over 30% of music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of platform play counts.
